The test blade had three rows of film holes on the leading edge and two rows each on the pressure and suction surfaces.
The mainstream Reynolds number based on the blade axial chord was 5.3 x 10^5.
Unsteady wakes were simulated using a spoke-wheel type wake generator upstream of the five-blade linear cascade.
Coolant blowing ratio was varied from 0.4 to 1.2 for the turbine blade experiments.
Higher density coolant (CO2) provided higher film cooling effectiveness at higher blowing ratios (M=1.2).
Lower density coolant (air) provided higher film cooling effectiveness at lower blowing ratios (M=0.8).
An increase in free-stream turbulence intensity (up to 7%) reduced film effectiveness significantly at low blowing ratios.
The film temperature distributions were measured using a cold-wire technique.
Unsteady wakes were found to significantly reduce film cooling effectiveness on the turbine blades.
Unsteady wakes slightly enhanced heat transfer coefficients but significantly reduced film cooling effectiveness on the turbine blades.
Trailing edge coolant ejection further enhanced the blade surface heat transfer coefficients, particularly near the leading edge region.
Trailing edge coolant ejection had more effect on film effectiveness distribution than on the heat transfer coefficients.
Film injection enhanced local heat transfer coefficients while the unsteady wake promoted earlier boundary-layer transition.
Higher density coolant (CO2) provided lower Nusselt numbers at all blowing ratios compared to lower density coolant (air).
An increase in free-stream turbulence had very small effect on Nusselt numbers for both air and CO2 coolants.
